# marcioaltoe/skills: require `typesafe-ai` and `crafting-effective-readmes` more widely; `lesson-learned` removed

Informational for Roundfix to act on; the skills repository expects no reply.
All three changes ship in the same skills PR and reach the Baseline through
the next asset sync.

| Skill                        | Change in skills                     | Presets                                 |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------- |
| `lesson-learned`             | `removed`                            | was only in `skill-authoring`           |
| `crafting-effective-readmes` | added to the Go and Rust presets     | now also `go-cli`, `go-tui`, `rust-cli` |
| `typesafe-ai`                | unchanged; already in all 10 presets | every Baseline setup already lists it   |

## Requests

1. **Require `typesafe-ai` in the `core` module.** It is in every setup
   snapshot, but the Baseline installs only skills a module requires, and no
   module requires it, so Roundfix-managed repositories never get it. The
   goal is that every project can use Jev (TypeSafe). Add it to
   `core.requiredSkills` with a dispatch trigger, for example
   `trigger.core.typesafe-ai`: "Adding programmable semantic judgment
   (routing, ranking, extraction, verification) or touching TypeSafe/Jev."
2. **Require `crafting-effective-readmes` for Go and Rust projects.** Today
   only the `typescript` module requires and dispatches it
   (`trigger.typescript.crafting-effective-readmes`: "Writing or revising the
   TypeScript repository README."). Add it to the `go` and `rust` modules'
   `requiredSkills` with matching triggers, or move it to `core`, since every
   built-in profile includes `core` and every Baseline setup now lists the
   skill.
3. **`lesson-learned` removed.** One recorded load across all session logs
   (2026-04-27). No Baseline setup or module names it, so no Roundfix change
   is expected.

## Sources

- https://github.com/marcioaltoe/skills/pull/103

# marcioaltoe/skills removes `review`; drop it from the Baseline

Informational for Roundfix to validate its Baseline; the skills repository
expects no reply. Unlike a passive removal, this one needs work in Roundfix: the
Baseline names `review` in every setup snapshot and in the `core` module.

| Old slug | New slug  | Presets that named it                                                                   |
| -------- | --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `review` | `removed` | `context-workflow`, `go-cli`, `go-tui`, `rust-cli`, `skill-authoring`, `typescript-bun` |

## Why

`review` was a frozen local copy of Matt Pocock's two-axis review skill
(Standards + Spec), which upstream renamed to `code-review` on 2026-07-01.
Nothing used it: no Roundfix skill or code path loads it, the `roundfix review`
command is unrelated, and the only Baseline link is the passive
`trigger.core.review` dispatch hint. The catalog therefore removes it instead
of following the rename. Neither `review` nor `code-review` exists in the
catalog, and no replacement is planned.

## What Roundfix needs to change

- Setup snapshots: refresh
  `internal/baseline/assets/setups/{go-cli,go-tui,rust-cli,typescript-bun}.json`
  through the asset sync once the skills PR merges; each lists
  `skills/06-review-repair/review`.
- `internal/baseline/assets/modules/core.json`: remove the `review` dispatch
  and `trigger.core.review`; do not rename it to `code-review`.
- Generated or golden docs that list that dispatch, such as
  `internal/baseline/assets/formatter-fixtures/standard-typescript-monorepo/golden/docs/agents/skill-dispatch.md`
  and the repository's own `docs/agents/skill-dispatch.md`.
- Roundfix's own install: `skills-lock.json` and `.agents/skills/review/`.
- Per ADR 0191, Roundfix never deletes an adopter's installed skill tree;
  adopters keep `.agents/skills/review/` until they remove it.

## Sources

- https://github.com/marcioaltoe/skills/pull/103

# marcioaltoe/skills removes `triage`; move its role into `external-triage`

Informational for Roundfix to act on; the skills repository expects no reply.
This removal needs Baseline work: the `typescript` module requires and
dispatches the skill.

| Old slug | New slug  | Presets that named it | Baseline setup snapshots |
| -------- | --------- | --------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `triage` | `removed` | `typescript-bun`      | `typescript-bun`         |

## Why

`triage` was Matt Pocock's issue/PR triage skill. It no longer fit:

- It depends on `setup-matt-pocock-skills` for the map from its roles to real
  tracker labels ("If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`"),
  and the catalog removed that skill with the `matt-pocock-workflow` preset.
- It routes accepted work to a `ready-for-agent` state with an agent brief,
  while Roundfix routes implementation through the repository's Spec policy.
- It sets `disable-model-invocation: true`, so the dispatch hint never
  auto-loads it in Claude Code.
- Roundfix already owns the domain through the `external-triage` module
  (`docs/agents/external-triage.md`, decision `triage.external`).

## What Roundfix needs to change

Removal:

- `internal/baseline/assets/modules/typescript.json`: drop `triage` from
  `requiredSkills` and remove the `trigger.typescript.triage` dispatch.
- Refresh `internal/baseline/assets/setups/typescript-bun.json` through the
  asset sync once the skills PR merges.
- Update the golden
  `formatter-fixtures/standard-typescript-monorepo/golden/docs/agents/skill-dispatch.md`
  and the parity fixture `testdata/parity-corpus/v1/fixtures/asset-sync.json`
  that list it.

Replacement: the `external-triage` guide is one rule today. Decide which of
the removed skill's functions it should own so external triage keeps working
without the skill:

- Classify each item (`bug` or `enhancement`) and move it through states
  (`needs-triage`, `needs-info`, ready, `wontfix`), mapped to the forge's real
  labels by the `triage.external` decision.
- For `needs-info`, ask the reporter specific questions and stop until they
  answer.
- Start every comment Roundfix posts on the forge with a disclaimer that AI
  generated it.
- Record `wontfix` decisions so repeated requests get the same answer (the
  skill used a `.out-of-scope/` knowledge base).
- Treat an external PR as an issue with attached code, with the same states.
- Route accepted work into the Spec workflow, not into an agent brief.

## Sources

- https://github.com/marcioaltoe/skills/pull/103
- Removed skill as last vendored:
  https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/tree/main/skills/engineering/triage

# marcioaltoe/skills removes 54 unused skills and the matt-pocock-workflow preset

Informational for Roundfix to validate its Baseline; the skills repository
expects no reply. No Baseline module requires or dispatches any of these
skills, so the next asset sync refresh is the only expected change: the
snapshots drop the rows below.

| Old slug                        | New slug  | Baseline setup snapshots that list it |
| ------------------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `accessibility`                 | `removed` | `typescript-bun`                      |
| `best-practices`                | `removed` | `typescript-bun`                      |
| `performance`                   | `removed` | `typescript-bun`                      |
| `web-quality-audit`             | `removed` | `typescript-bun`                      |
| `firecrawl-developer-index`     | `removed` | `typescript-bun`                      |
| `firecrawl-monitor`             | `removed` | `typescript-bun`                      |
| `firecrawl-research-index`      | `removed` | `typescript-bun`                      |
| `golang-benchmark`              | `removed` | `go-cli`, `go-tui`                    |
| `golang-continuous-integration` | `removed` | `go-cli`, `go-tui`                    |
| `golang-database`               | `removed` | `go-cli`, `go-tui`                    |
| `golang-modernize`              | `removed` | `go-cli`, `go-tui`                    |
| `golang-observability`          | `removed` | `go-cli`, `go-tui`                    |
| `golang-performance`            | `removed` | `go-cli`, `go-tui`                    |

The other 41 removed skills appear in no Baseline setup. They are 22
marketing skills, the devops and docs skills (`aws-architecture-diagram`,
`deploy`, `elastic-beanstalk`, `refactor-module`, `terraform-search-import`,
`terraform-test`, `sentry`, `mermaid-studio`, `professional-communication`),
and the Matt Pocock workflow skills (`ask-matt`, `improve-codebase-architecture`,
`prototype`, `teach`, `to-spec`, `to-tickets`, `wayfinder`, `implement`,
`grill-me`, `setup-matt-pocock-skills`). The `matt-pocock-workflow` preset is
gone; it was never a Baseline setup.

Why: across 5,275 Codex sessions since April 2026, including Roundfix runs, and
the retained Claude Code sessions, no agent ever loaded these skills. Skills
the Baseline modules depend on stay even with no recorded use (`context7-cli`,
`business-storyteller`, `game-changing-features`, `design-patterns`, `motion`,
`fixing-motion-performance`, `core-web-vitals`, `clap-rust`, `rust-expert`).

The same PR adds nine `gws-*` Google Workspace skills to the `docs` preset,
which is not a Baseline setup.

# marcioaltoe/skills renames its setup presets: `go`, `rust`, `typescript`

Informational for Roundfix to act on; the skills repository expects no reply.
These are preset (setup) renames, not skill renames; no skill slug changes. The
next Baseline asset sync breaks until Roundfix repoints its setup snapshots,
because the old `setups/*.txt` files no longer exist on `main`.

| Old preset       | New preset   | Roundfix profile that uses it  | Notes                                                         |
| ---------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `go-tui`         | `go`         | `go-cli-tui`                   | Same skill list (Go CLI + `bubbletea` + `tui-design`)         |
| `go-cli`         | `removed`    | none (snapshot used in tests)  | Was `go` minus `bubbletea` and `tui-design`; merged into `go` |
| `rust-cli`       | `rust`       | `rust-cli`                     | Same skill list; the `rust-cli` skill keeps its name          |
| `typescript-bun` | `typescript` | `standard-typescript-monorepo` | Same skill list                                               |

The same PR also removes the `docs`, `marketing`, `release`,
`context-workflow`, and `skill-authoring` presets, merging `docs` and
`marketing` into a new `content` preset. No Roundfix profile uses any of them.

## What Roundfix needs to change

- Profiles: set `setup` to `go` in `profiles/go-cli-tui.json`, `rust` in
  `profiles/rust-cli.json`, and `typescript` in
  `profiles/standard-typescript-monorepo.json`.
- Setup snapshots: replace `assets/setups/{go-tui,rust-cli,typescript-bun}.json`
  with `{go,rust,typescript}.json` sourced from `setups/{go,rust,typescript}.txt`,
  and retire `assets/setups/go-cli.json`. Tests that load `setups/go-cli.json`
  (for example `catalog_test.go`, `assets_sync_test.go`,
  `assets_sync_owned_membership_test.go`, `derived_ownership_test.go`) need a
  new fixture or the `go` snapshot.
- Source baselines and parity data that name the old setup ids, such as `source-baselines/baseline.standard-typescript-monorepo-0.0.1/`,
  and the parity-corpus fixtures.
- Active Spec 0207 ("a Go CLI and a TypeScript monorepo in one baseline")
  names `typescript-bun` and the Go setups; align it with the new ids.
- Roundfix-owned skills vendored into the catalog that name a setup, such as
  `skills/roundfix/references/baseline.md`, follow on their next sync.

## Sources

- https://github.com/marcioaltoe/skills/pull/103

# Triage Labels

The skills speak in terms of five canonical triage roles. This file maps those roles to the actual label strings used in this repo's issue tracker.

| Label in mattpocock/skills | Label in our tracker | Meaning                                  |
| -------------------------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `needs-triage`             | `needs-triage`       | Maintainer needs to evaluate this issue  |
| `needs-info`               | `needs-info`         | Waiting on reporter for more information |
| `ready-for-agent`          | `ready-for-agent`    | Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent  |
| `ready-for-human`          | `ready-for-human`    | Requires human implementation            |
| `wontfix`                  | `wontfix`            | Will not be actioned                     |

When a skill mentions a role, use the corresponding label string from this table.

Edit the right-hand column to match whatever vocabulary you actually use.
